newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Bolger says intends being at APEC summit.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Bolger says intends being at APEC summit.

text.p: Prime Minister Jim Bolger on Friday confirmed he intended to be at the regional leaders' summit in Manila later in November if his caretaker government was still in place.

Labour leader Helen Clark said on Thursday the government had "no authority at all" to send Bolger to the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation forum's summit due to be held in the Philippines capital on November 25.

But the New Zealand Press Association reported Bolger as saying that despite his government's caretaker status since the equivocal October 12 election result, he was still the prime minister and it was important New Zealand be represented at the summit.
NZPA understands Bolger intends taking an RNZAF plane to the Philippines, flying up the day before the summit and returning the day after.

The 18-strong Apec forum groups the most influential countries of the Pacific rim, including the United States, Japan, China, Canada, Mexico, Australia and the so-called South-East Asian "tiger" economies.
The one-day summit provides an unparalleled opportunity for the leaders to meet, renew and extend personal relationships.
"It's a hugely important conference and barring exceptional circumstances, New Zealand will be represented," Bolger said.
Despite other parties' calls for consultation, and Clark's claim that his government had no authority, in fact his ministers were entitled to attend forums like Apec, he said.
"The prime minister is the prime minister and the ministers are the ministers. They have the warrant, they've sworn an oath of office.
"There is only one person who has the responsibility that goes with the office of prime minister," Bolger said, adding that no-one except the prime minister could attend the Apec leaders' summit.
When US President Bill Clinton was unable to attend Apec last year, he did not send his deputy to fill in.
Bolger said that although there was no obligation on him to consult Clark about his attendance at Apec, he was more than happy to talk to the other leaders about it.

"The good thing is that other than the Alliance, who seem to have some rather quirky ideas on trade policy, the other two parties have broadly similar trade policies (to National) so it's not an area where you will find huge political difficulties, with the qualification of the Alliance."
The summit is preceded by a meeting of foreign affairs ministers which Don McKinnon will attend if the caretaker government is still in place.

There is also a meeting of trade ministers but retiring Trade Negotiations Minister Philip Burdon will have handed in his warrant by then so it was possible McKinnon would also attend on Burdon's behalf, Bolger said.
